title: Logistics Note: Delivery Charging Where a Catering Site Sits on a Standing Round
content:
A site the vans already call at costs less to serve than a fresh address. The delivery charge raised on an order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement therefore turns on the agreement's delivery record over the 12 months ending on the day the invoice is raised and on whether the order went to the site named on the agreement.

**First**, where the agreement carried 5 or more deliveries in the 12 months ending on the day the invoice is raised and the order was delivered to the site named on the agreement, no delivery charge at all is raised, the site sitting on a standing round.

**Second**, where the agreement carried 2 or more deliveries in those 12 months and the order was delivered to the site named on the agreement, the charge is half — that is 0.5, or 50 per cent — of the fee printed against the catering service level.

**Otherwise**, the charge is the fee printed against the catering service level.

| Deliveries in the 12 months ending on the day the invoice is raised | Order delivered to the site named on the agreement | Delivery charge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 or more | yes | none |
| 5 or more | no | the fee printed against the service level |
| At least 2 and fewer than 5 | yes | half the fee printed against the service level |
| At least 2 and fewer than 5 | no | the fee printed against the service level |
| Fewer than 2 | either way | the fee printed against the service level |

### Both sides of the counts

On a hypothetical agreement whose service level is printed with a delivery fee of 55.00 USD and whose order went to the site named on the agreement: a delivery record of exactly 5 in those 12 months carries no charge; a record of 4 carries 27.50 USD; a record of exactly 2 carries 27.50 USD; and a record of 1 carries the whole 55.00 USD. Where the same order went to an address other than the site named on the agreement, the charge is 55.00 USD whatever the delivery record shows.
